advances: Actual median-pair couplings with proportional central splitting. The atom alignment applies to the retained part at the displaced center.

proof:
Each source marginal has constant density on each fiber. The retained restrictions therefore have translated marginals bounded by $\alpha,\beta$. The deficits have common mass $e$ and can be coupled by their product divided by $e$ if $e>0$, or by the zero measure otherwise. Adding this coupling to the translated retained pairs gives $\sigma_{h,b}$. The interpolation coefficients in $T$ add to one and have mean base $z_0$, so $T(Qp,Qq)=T(p,q)+h$. This identity also holds for a pair of central endpoints. Thus the new and translated old midpoint laws share the whole translated retained part, and their unmatched measures each have mass $e$. The union bound and $\alpha+\beta=2\mu$ give the displayed bound on $e$.

The endpoint supports are compact and $T$ is continuous on each of the finitely many clopen base-pair strata, hence continuous on their product. Compactness and the upper semicontinuity of closed-cap integrals give attainment at each fixed center, as in a16dfa31498230d5. For $y\in K_{z_0}$, finite approximation and the weighted dual of 0aaf1194bb28ee86 give $V(y)=\inf J(y)$. For $y\notin K_{z_0}$, strict separation provides a through-$y$ cap missing the fiber, giving both the zero depth and the zero infimum. For any chosen coupling, the exact translation of the retained part aligns every closed through-center cap, including its boundary. A test taking values in $[0,1]$, such as any finite weighted cap mixture, changes by at most $e$ after aligning the two centers. The same holds for the infimum of the individual cap masses. Apply this to the optimizer at $y$ and, using $(-h,-b)$, to the optimizer at $y+h$. The overlap bound is symmetric under reversing every fiber shift, so it controls the absolute differences. This holds for every $b$.

For a unit vector $u$, write the slices of $K_z$ parallel to $u$ as intervals $I_s$ indexed by $s\in u^\perp$. The loss under translation by $au$ on each interval is $\min(|a|,|I_s|)$, including empty or singleton slices. Integrating gives $|K_z|-|K_z\cap(K_z-au)|\le |a|\operatorname{vol}_{d-1}(\operatorname{proj}_{u^\perp}K_z)$. For the displacement $th$ use the shear $tb$ and this inequality, then take the infimum over $b$. In particular choosing $b=0$ and bounding all projected volumes by those of a common containing ball gives a Lipschitz constant independent of the cap mixture.
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, be compact and convex with positive mixed volume $M=\sum_z|K_z|$. Let $\mu$ be normalized mixed volume, and choose an integer median base $z_0$. Split the measure at $z_0$ proportionally so that the two sides, each including its assigned central share, have mass $1/2$. Double those measures to obtain probability marginals $\alpha,\beta$ with $\alpha+\beta=2\mu$. For a legal pair $p=(i,x),q=(j,y)$, put
$$
T(p,q)=\begin{cases}
[(j-z_0)x+(z_0-i)y]/(j-i),&i<j,\\
(x+y)/2,&i=j=z_0 .
\end{cases}
$$
By convexity this is in the actual fiber $K_{z_0}$.

For $h,b\in\mathbb R^d$ let $Q$ translate each fiber's continuous coordinate by $h_z=h+(z-z_0)b$. From any probability coupling $\sigma$ of $\alpha,\beta$, one can retain the subcoupling of pairs for which both translated endpoints stay in their fibers, translate it by $(Q,Q)$, and complete to a coupling $\sigma_{h,b}$ of $\alpha,\beta$. The retained midpoint law is translated by exactly $h$, including its atoms. The total variation distance between $T_\#\sigma_{h,b}$ and the translate of $T_\#\sigma$ by $h$, using $\sup_A|\rho(A)-\rho'(A)|$, is at most the discarded mass $e$, where
$$
e\le \min\!\left(1,\frac2M\sum_z[|K_z|-|K_z\cap(K_z-h_z)|]\right).
$$

Write $V(y)$ for the maximum closed-halfspace depth at $y$ over these targets, and $J(y)$ for the maximum over the same couplings of any finite nonnegative weighted average of through-$y$ closed cap masses with weights summing to one. Then $V(y)$ is the infimum of $J(y)$ over all such finite cap mixtures. Both $V$ and every $J$ obey the preceding displacement bound in absolute value after taking the infimum over $b$. In particular, for any $t\in\mathbb R$ and $h\in\mathbb R^d$, the displacement $th$ changes both values by at most
$$
|t|\,\frac2M\inf_{b\in\mathbb R^d}\sum_z P_z(h+(z-z_0)b),
\qquad
P_z(v)=|v|\operatorname{vol}_{d-1}(\operatorname{proj}_{v^\perp}K_z)\quad(v\ne0),
$$
with $P_z(0)=0$, and the nonempty projection of an interval in $d=1$ has zero-dimensional volume one. The sums can be restricted to positive-volume fibers.
title: Atom-preserving median coupling exchange under a fiber shear
